common_name: Prelude Raspberry (Very Early Cold-Hardy Summer-Bearing Red Raspberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or potted plants in early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a trellis or support wires for the upright canes.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil enriched with compost, in full sun, and support upright canes with a trellis or wire system. Prelude was bred at Cornell University's New York research station for exceptionally early ripening, opening the summer raspberry season days to weeks ahead of most other floricane (summer-bearing) varieties, a genuine advantage for gardeners eager for the first fresh raspberries of the year. The medium-sized, firm, richly flavored red berries are borne on vigorous, cold-hardy canes well suited to northern growing conditions. Prune out spent floricanes after harvest each summer to make room for new cane growth, and thin canes to the strongest four to six per foot of row for the best fruit size and air circulation.

common_name: Amity Raspberry (Large Fall-Bearing Oregon Red Raspberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or potted plants in early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; as a fall-bearing (primocane) type, Amity can be mowed to the ground each winter for a single simplified fall crop.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil enriched with compost, in full sun, providing support for canes as they fill in. Amity was bred at Oregon State University as a fall-bearing (primocane) red raspberry, producing large, firm, richly flavored berries on the current season's new canes from late summer through fall, well after most summer-bearing varieties have finished. Because primocane types fruit on new growth, the entire planting can be mowed or cut to the ground each winter, radically simplifying pruning compared to summer-bearing varieties that require selective cane removal. This makes Amity a particularly low-maintenance choice for home gardeners wanting a single, reliable, high-quality fall raspberry crop without the more involved care summer-bearing brambles need.

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or potted plants in early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a sturdy trellis to support the very heavy fruit clusters.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil enriched with compost, in full sun, and stake or trellis canes securely to support the exceptionally heavy fruit. Titan is an English-bred summer-bearing red raspberry known for producing some of the largest raspberry fruit commonly grown, with individual berries noticeably bigger than most standard varieties, making it popular for exhibition growing as well as home fresh eating. The vigorous, thorny canes are productive and reliable, though the sheer size and weight of the fruit clusters make sturdy support more important than with smaller-fruited varieties, since overloaded canes can bend or break without it. Prune out spent floricanes after harvest each summer, and thin new canes to the strongest for the best fruit size the following season.

common_name: Nordic Raspberry (Extremely Cold-Hardy Minnesota Fall-Bearing Raspberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or potted plants in early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; exceptionally cold-hardy and well adapted to zones 3-7, as a fall-bearing type it can be mowed to the ground each winter.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil enriched with compost, in full sun. Nordic was bred at the University of Minnesota specifically for extreme cold hardiness, giving it a genuine advantage in the harshest northern growing regions where many other raspberry varieties suffer significant winter cane damage or fail outright. As a fall-bearing (primocane) type producing fruit on the current season's new canes, it can be cut entirely to the ground each winter, a simple, low-maintenance pruning approach well suited to gardeners in cold climates who want a reliable, straightforward raspberry crop without fussing over selective cane pruning. The compact, sturdy canes produce good yields of flavorful red berries from late summer into fall, right up until hard frost ends the season.

common_name: Himbo Top Raspberry (Productive Swiss Fall-Bearing Raspberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or potted plants in early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; as a fall-bearing type, Himbo Top can be mowed to the ground each winter for simplified pruning.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil enriched with compost, in full sun, and provide support for the tall, productive canes. Himbo Top was bred in Switzerland (its name drawn from the German word for raspberry, 'Himbeere') as a fall-bearing red raspberry, and it has become popular with commercial growers and home gardeners alike for combining very heavy yields with large, firm, well-flavored berries that hold their shape and quality well after picking. Producing fruit on current-season canes from late summer into fall, it can be managed with the simple annual mow-down pruning typical of primocane raspberries, making it a practical, high-yielding choice for gardeners who want strong production without complex cane management. Pick regularly during the fall fruiting window, since the heavy-bearing canes can set fruit faster than a light picking schedule can keep up with.
